admission.justification: The construction lives in the two entry points and the inputs object of the worktrees module, which the controller and the closeout adapter must call; the new module's grouped, singleton and malformed cases prove that one row answers the worklist item and both gates raise it.

applicability: Every onboarding_trace item the memory-quality run and the closeout validator build for a leaf on a converted memory worktree.
conditions: The entry is given a complete worklist run's identicalChanges mapping, whose entries map a representative source path to the source paths of its identical copies.
The worklist run was built for the candidate the entry judges.
exclusions: The worklist's own item construction and the item-id contract are unchanged.
An entry that cannot read a complete run's groups refuses by name instead of judging ungrouped items.

evidence: test_one_row_binding_every_copy...: the ten-copy card closed in the worklist is closed by both entries with the worklist's own two item ids and no finding; freeze-a02/probe-candidate.log: the candidate raises the worklist's ten-source item (sha256:280c0519…) where A01 raised the singleton (freeze/freeze-a02 probe-a01.log). Candidate tree 6868e51d.

test_the_quality_run_refuses_by_name_when_the_worklist_run_names_no_groups: a complete run closes both items and an incomplete or absent run returns one onboarding-trace-incomplete finding naming the worklist file, with no ungrouped item.

statement: The memory-quality onboarding gate and the closeout onboarding validator build their onboarding_trace items from the leaf worklist run's own identicalChanges groups, so an item a row answers in the worklist is the item both entries raise.
